S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) is characterized by developmentally inappropriate levels of motor activity, impulsivity, and difficulty inhibiting responses, with comparatively fewer or less prominent inattentive symptoms. Individuals often present with restlessness, difficulty remaining seated, interrupting others, and acting without considering consequences, which must cause impairment in at least two settings and be present for a prolonged period. In adults, the clinical picture may shift from overt hyperactivity toward inner restlessness and chronic impulsive decision-making, often impacting work performance, relationships, and safety. It is distinguished from anxiety disorders, bipolar spectrum conditions, and personality disorders by its early neurodevelopmental origins, pervasive pattern across contexts, and lack of sustained mood episodes, with symptoms typically fluctuating in intensity depending on demands rather than appearing episodically.

patient.personality: He is an energetic, curiosity-driven teacher who thrives on spontaneous, hands-on activities but struggles to rein in his own momentum and stay organized when demands pile up.
patient.stressor: Roughly two years ago, Michael and his spouse welcomed their second child, which coincided with him taking on additional responsibilities at school, including leading STEM initiatives and coaching Little League. The combination of increased family duties, disrupted sleep, and extra roles that required long planning meetings and careful coordination made his long-standing restlessness and impulsive style far more problematic, as he found it harder to remain calmly present during family time and structured school activities. At home, his spouse became increasingly frustrated that he seemed unable to sit through meals, bedtime routines, or quiet evenings without pacing, fiddling with gadgets, or abruptly changing the topic or activity, which led to arguments about whether he was truly engaged with the family. At school, colleagues began commenting on his inability to stay seated during committees and his tendency to jump in before others finished speaking, and after a particularly tense parent conference where his constant movement was misread as disinterest, he agreed—at his spouse’s strong encouragement—to consult a psychiatrist to understand why his behavior was straining both his marriage and his professional relationships.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’m constantly fidgeting and can’t seem to sit still at home or at school, and it’s starting to cause problems with my family and coworkers.”

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: Lately I’ve been sending home newsletters with wrong dates or missing steps in assignments because I skim what I’ve typed, miss obvious typos, and only realize it when a parent emails me confused or my wife points out I’ve double-booked us on the family calendar again.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: My wife will be telling me about a rough day with the kids or my principal will be giving instructions in a staff meeting, and halfway through I realize I’ve drifted off into thinking about a new science project or tomorrow’s lineup, so I end up asking them to repeat things they literally just said.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: Whether I’m at the dinner table, in a parent conference, or sitting on the couch for a kids’ movie, my legs are bouncing nonstop, my fingers are drumming on whatever’s in reach, and I’m constantly shifting around to the point where my daughter now tells me, ‘Daddy, stop shaking the table.’

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: In long meetings or even during family dinner I’ll suddenly stand up under the excuse of refilling my coffee or checking something in the classroom or kitchen, and before I know it I’m pacing or straightening things while people are still talking and expecting me to be seated with them.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Anytime I’m supposed to just sit still—like bedtime stories with the kids, staff development days, or even church—I feel this pent-up energy crawling under my skin, like I physically can’t stay put and have to keep shifting, stretching, or looking for some little task to do just to get through it.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: From the minute I wake up until I crash at night, I’m bouncing from prepping lessons to fixing something in the garage to answering emails to planning Little League drills, and even when my wife begs me to just sit and watch a show, my brain is already pulling me toward the next thing I “need” to do.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: In team meetings and parent conferences I catch myself jumping in with answers or solutions before the other person has even finished their sentence, and I’ve had colleagues visibly bristle when I cut them off with, ‘Yeah, yeah, I know where you’re going with this,’ even when I don’t.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I’m constantly barging into other teachers’ classrooms with ideas while they’re trying to work, chiming into conversations in the staff room that I wasn’t part of, and at home I’ll talk over my wife’s stories or jump into the kids’ games uninvited, then realize from their faces that I’ve steamrolled everyone again.
